questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $\alpha,\ \alpha+2$, $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}$, be the roots of the quadratic equation $x(x+2)+(x+1)(x+3)+(x+2)(x+4)+\dots+(x+n-1)(x+n+1)=4n$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $n+\alpha$ is equal to:
questions.explanation: The sum is $nx^2+n(n+1)x+\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(k^2+2k)$, so the equation is $nx^2+n(n+1)x+S-4n=0$. Roots differ by 2, so $(\text{sum})^2-4(\text{product})=4$: $(n+1)^2-\frac{4(S-4n)}{n}=4$, which gives $n=7$. Sum of roots $2\alpha+2=-(n+1)=-8\Rightarrow\alpha=-5$, so $n+\alpha=2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$ be such that the system of linear equations $x+2y+z=5$, $2x+y+\alpha z=5$, $8x+4y+\beta z=18$ has no solution. Then $\dfrac{\beta}{\alpha}$ is equal to:
questions.explanation: No solution needs $\Delta=0$: $\begin{vmatrix}1&2&1\\2&1&\alpha\\8&4&\beta\end{vmatrix}=12\alpha-3\beta=0$, so $\beta=4\alpha$ and $\frac{\beta}{\alpha}=4$ (the third equation then contradicts the first two).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\1&\alpha\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}3&3\\\beta&2\end{bmatrix}$. If $A^2-4A+I=O$ and $B^2-5B-6I=O$, then among the two statements (S1): $[(B-A)(B+A)]^T=\begin{bmatrix}13&15\\7&10\end{bmatrix}$ and (S2): $\det(\operatorname{adj}(A+B))=-5$,
questions.explanation: By Cayley–Hamilton, $\operatorname{tr}A=4\Rightarrow\alpha=3$ and $\det B=-6\Rightarrow 6-3\beta=-6\Rightarrow\beta=4$. Then $(B-A)(B+A)=\begin{bmatrix}13&15\\7&10\end{bmatrix}$, whose transpose is $\begin{bmatrix}13&7\\15&10\end{bmatrix}$, so (S1) is wrong. For a $2\times2$ matrix $\det(\operatorname{adj}M)=\det M$, and $\det(A+B)=\begin{vmatrix}4&5\\5&5\end{vmatrix}=-5$, so (S2) is correct.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $A$ be the set of first 101 terms of an A.P., whose first term is 1 and the common difference is 5 and let $B$ be the set of first 71 terms of an A.P., whose first term is 9 and the common difference is 7. Then the number of elements in $A\cap B$, which are divisible by 3, is:
questions.explanation: $A=\{1,6,\dots,501\}$, $B=\{9,16,\dots,499\}$. Common terms satisfy $x\equiv1\pmod5$ and $x\equiv2\pmod7$: $x=16,51,86,\dots$ (difference 35) up to 499, i.e. $16+35m$ for $m=0,\dots,13$. Divisible by 3 needs $16+35m\equiv0\pmod 3\Rightarrow m\equiv1\pmod3$: $m=1,4,7,10,13$ — 5 numbers.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The number of seven-digit numbers, that can be formed by using the digits 1, 2, 3, 5 and 7 such that each digit is used at least once, is:
questions.explanation: Count onto maps from 7 places to 5 digits (inclusion–exclusion): $5^7-\binom51 4^7+\binom52 3^7-\binom53 2^7+\binom54 1^7=78125-81920+21870-1280+5=16800$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the mean of the data — class: 5–10, 10–15, 15–20, 20–25, 25–30, 30–35; frequency: 2, $k$, 28, 54, $k+1$, 5 — is 21, then $k$ is one of the roots of the equation:
questions.explanation: Using mid-values $7.5,12.5,\dots,32.5$: $\sum f_ix_i=1910+40k$ and $\sum f_i=90+2k$. Mean $21\Rightarrow1910+40k=1890+42k\Rightarrow k=10$, and $x=10$ satisfies $2x^2-19x-10=200-190-10=0$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let the mid points of the sides of a triangle ABC be $\left(\frac52,7\right)$, $\left(\frac52,3\right)$ and $(4,5)$. If its incentre is $(h,k)$, then $3h+k$ is equal to:
questions.explanation: Vertices are $D+E-F$ type sums: $(4,1)$, $(4,9)$ and $(1,5)$. Side lengths opposite them: $a=5$, $b=5$, $c=8$. Incentre $=\frac{5(4,1)+5(4,9)+8(1,5)}{18}=\left(\frac83,5\right)$, so $3h+k=8+5=13$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let an ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$, $a<b$, pass through the point $(4,3)$ and have eccentricity $\dfrac{\sqrt5}{3}$. Then the length of its latus rectum is:
questions.explanation: Major axis is along $y$: $a^2=b^2(1-e^2)=\frac{4b^2}{9}$. From $(4,3)$: $\frac{36}{b^2}+\frac{9}{b^2}=1\Rightarrow b^2=45$, $a^2=20$. Latus rectum $=\frac{2a^2}{b}=\frac{40}{3\sqrt5}=\frac{8\sqrt5}{3}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{18}\right)\sin\left(\frac{5\pi}{18}\right)\sin\left(\frac{7\pi}{18}\right)=K$, then the value of $\sin\left(\frac{10K\pi}{3}\right)$ is:
questions.explanation: $\sin10^\circ\sin50^\circ\sin70^\circ=\sin\theta\sin(60^\circ-\theta)\sin(60^\circ+\theta)=\frac14\sin30^\circ=\frac18$ with $\theta=10^\circ$. So $\sin\frac{10\pi}{24}=\sin75^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3+1}{2\sqrt2}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $S=\{x\in[-\pi,\pi]:\sin x(\sin x+\cos x)=a,\ a\in\mathbb{Z}\}$. Then $n(S)$ is equal to:
questions.explanation: $\sin^2x+\sin x\cos x=\frac12+\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\sin\left(2x-\frac\pi4\right)\in\left[\frac{1-\sqrt2}{2},\frac{1+\sqrt2}{2}\right]$, so $a\in\{0,1\}$. $a=0$: $\sin x=0$ ($-\pi,0,\pi$) or $\tan x=-1$ ($-\frac\pi4,\frac{3\pi}4$) — 5. $a=1$: $\cos x(\sin x-\cos x)=0$ gives $\pm\frac\pi2,\frac\pi4,-\frac{3\pi}4$ — 4. Total 9.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the point of intersection of the lines $\dfrac{x+1}{3}=\dfrac{y+a}{5}=\dfrac{z+b+1}{7}$ and $\dfrac{x-2}{1}=\dfrac{y-b}{4}=\dfrac{z-2a}{7}$ lies on $xy$-plane, then the value of $a+b$ is:
questions.explanation: General points: $(3t-1,\,5t-a,\,7t-b-1)$ and $(s+2,\,4s+b,\,7s+2a)$. Equating and using $z=0$ gives $t=\frac57$, $s=-\frac67$, $a=3$, $b=4$, so $a+b=7$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ are two vectors such that $|\vec a|=2$ and $|\vec b|=3$, then the maximum value of $3\left|3\vec a+2\vec b\right|+4\left|3\vec a-2\vec b\right|$ is:
questions.explanation: $|3\vec a\pm2\vec b|^2=36+36\pm12\,\vec a\cdot\vec b=72(1\pm\cos\theta)$, so the expression is $12\sqrt2\left(3\sqrt{1+\cos\theta}+4\sqrt{1-\cos\theta}\right)=24\left(3\cos\frac\theta2+4\sin\frac\theta2\right)\le24\cdot5=60$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let a line L passing through the point $(1,1,1)$ be perpendicular to both the vectors $2\hat i+2\hat j+\hat k$ and $\hat i+2\hat j+2\hat k$. If $P(a,b,c)$ is the foot of perpendicular from the origin on the line L, then the value of $34(a+b+c)$ is:
questions.explanation: Direction of L: $(2,2,1)\times(1,2,2)=(2,-3,2)$. Point on L: $(1+2\lambda,1-3\lambda,1+2\lambda)$; perpendicular from O needs $2(1+2\lambda)-3(1-3\lambda)+2(1+2\lambda)=0\Rightarrow\lambda=-\frac1{17}$. So $P=\left(\frac{15}{17},\frac{20}{17},\frac{15}{17}\right)$ and $34(a+b+c)=2\cdot50=100$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to2}\frac{\sin\left(x^3-5x^2+ax+b\right)}{\left(\sqrt{x-1}-1\right)\log_e(x-1)}=m$, then $a+b+m$ is equal to:
questions.explanation: The denominator behaves like $\frac{(x-2)}{2}\cdot(x-2)$, i.e. it has a double zero at $x=2$. A finite limit needs $p(x)=x^3-5x^2+ax+b$ to have a double root at 2: $p(2)=0$, $p'(2)=0\Rightarrow a=8$, $b=-4$. Then $p(x)=(x-2)^2(x-1)$ and $m=\lim\frac{(x-2)^2(x-1)}{(x-2)^2/2}=2$. So $a+b+m=6$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the curve $y=f(x)$ passes through the point $(1,e)$ and satisfies the differential equation $dy=y(2+\log_e x)\,dx$, $x>0$, then $f(e)$ is equal to:
questions.explanation: Separate: $\frac{dy}{y}=(2+\ln x)dx\Rightarrow\ln y=x+x\ln x+C$. At $(1,e)$: $1=1+C\Rightarrow C=0$. So $f(e)=e^{e+e}=e^{2e}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The number of critical points of the function $f(x)=\begin{cases}\left|\dfrac{\sin x}{x}\right|, & x\ne0\\ 1, & x=0\end{cases}$ in the interval $(-2\pi,2\pi)$ is equal to:
questions.explanation: $f$ is even and smooth at 0 with $f'(0)=0$ (critical). At $x=\pm\pi$, $f=0$ with a corner, so $f'$ does not exist (critical). Between $\pi$ and $2\pi$, $f'=0$ where $\tan x=x$ (one root, $x\approx4.49$), and likewise at $x\approx-4.49$. Total: $0,\pm\pi,\pm4.49$ — 5 points.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation $(1+\sin x)\dfrac{dy}{dx}+(y+1)\cos x=0$, $y(0)=0$. If the curve $y=y(x)$ passes through the point $\left(\alpha,-\frac12\right)$, then a value of $\alpha$ is:
questions.explanation: $\frac{d}{dx}\left[(y+1)(1+\sin x)\right]=0$, so $(y+1)(1+\sin x)=C=1$ (from $y(0)=0$). For $y=-\frac12$: $1+\sin\alpha=2\Rightarrow\alpha=\frac\pi2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the domain of the function $f(x)=\sqrt{\log_{(0.6)}\left(\left|\dfrac{2x-5}{x^2-4}\right|\right)}$ is $(-\infty,a]\cup\{b\}\cup[c,d)\cup(e,\infty)$, then the value of $a+b+c+d+e$ is ______.
questions.explanation: Need $0<\left|\frac{2x-5}{x^2-4}\right|\le1$ (base $0.6<1$), i.e. $|2x-5|\le|x^2-4|$ with $x\ne\pm2,\frac52$. Solving gives $(-\infty,-1-\sqrt{10}]\cup\{1\}\cup[\sqrt{10}-1,\frac52)\cup(\frac52,\infty)$. Sum $=(-1-\sqrt{10})+1+(\sqrt{10}-1)+\frac52+\frac52=4$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}a_k=6n^3$, then $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{6}\left(\frac{a_{k+1}-a_k}{36}\right)^2$ is equal to ______.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $a,b,c\in\{1,2,3,4\}$. If the probability that $ax^2+2\sqrt2\,bx+c>0$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}$ is $\dfrac mn$, $\gcd(m,n)=1$, then $m+n$ is equal to ______.
questions.explanation: Need $a>0$ (always) and discriminant $8b^2-4ac<0$, i.e. $ac>2b^2$. $b=1$: $ac>2$ — 13 pairs; $b=2$: $ac>8$ — 4 pairs; $b=3,4$: none. Favourable $=17$ of $64$, so $m+n=81$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let a circle C have its centre in the first quadrant, intersect the coordinate axes at exactly three points and cut off equal intercepts from the coordinate axes. If the length of the chord of C on the line $x+y=1$ is $\sqrt{14}$, then the square of the radius of C is ______.
questions.explanation: Equal intercepts put the centre at $(h,h)$; meeting the axes in exactly three points means it passes through the origin, so $r^2=2h^2$. Chord: $r^2-\frac{(2h-1)^2}{2}=\frac{14}{4}\Rightarrow 4h-1=7\Rightarrow h=2$, so $r^2=8$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\alpha=\displaystyle\int_0^{2\sqrt3}\log_2\left(x^2+4\right)dx+\int_2^4\sqrt{2^x-4}\,dx$, then $\alpha^2$ is equal to ______.
questions.explanation: $y=\log_2(x^2+4)$ and $x=\sqrt{2^y-4}$ are inverses, mapping $[0,2\sqrt3]$ onto $[2,4]$. The two areas together fill the rectangle: $\alpha=2\sqrt3\cdot4-0\cdot2=8\sqrt3$, so $\alpha^2=192$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The dimensional formula of $\frac12\epsilon_0E^2$ ($\epsilon_0$ = permittivity of vacuum and $E$ = electric field) is $M^aL^bT^c$. The value of $2a-b+c$ = ______.
questions.explanation: $\frac12\epsilon_0E^2$ is energy per unit volume: $[ML^{-1}T^{-2}]$. So $a=1,b=-1,c=-2$ and $2a-b+c=2+1-2=1$.

questions.text: A planet $(P_1)$ is moving around the star of mass $2M$ in the orbit of radius $R$. Another planet $(P_2)$ is moving around another star of mass $4M$ in a orbit of radius $2R$. Ratio of time periods of revolution of $P_2$ and $P_1$ is ______.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.text: A particle is rotating in a circular path and at any instant its motion can be described as $\theta=\dfrac{5t^4}{40}-\dfrac{t^3}{3}$. The angular acceleration of the particle after 10 seconds is ______ rad/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A parallel plate air capacitor has a capacitance C. When it is half filled as shown in figure with a dielectric constant $K=5$, the percentage increase in the capacitance is ______.
questions.explanation: The slab fills thickness $\frac d2$ over the whole plate area, so it acts in series with an air gap $\frac d2$: $C'=\frac{\epsilon_0A}{\frac d2+\frac{d}{2K}}=\frac{\epsilon_0A}{d}\cdot\frac{2K}{K+1}=\frac{5}{3}C$. Increase $=\frac23\times100\%=66.67\%$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Heat is supplied to a diatomic gas at constant pressure. Then the ratio of $\Delta Q:\Delta U:\Delta W$ is ______.
questions.explanation: At constant pressure $\Delta Q=nC_p\Delta T$, $\Delta U=nC_v\Delta T$, $\Delta W=nR\Delta T$. For a diatomic gas $C_p:C_v:R=\frac72R:\frac52R:R=7:5:2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two charged conducting spheres $S_1$ and $S_2$ of radii 8 cm and 18 cm are connected to each other by a wire. After equilibrium is established, the ratio of electric fields on $S_1$ and $S_2$ spheres are $E_{S1}$ and $E_{S2}$ respectively. The value of $\dfrac{E_{S1}}{E_{S2}}$ is ______.
questions.explanation: Connected spheres reach the same potential $V$. Surface field $E=\frac{kQ}{r^2}=\frac Vr$, so $\frac{E_1}{E_2}=\frac{r_2}{r_1}=\frac{18}{8}=\frac94$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The equation of a plane progressive wave is given by $y=5\cos\pi\left(200t-\dfrac{x}{150}\right)$ where $x$ and $y$ are in cm and $t$ is in second. The velocity of the wave is ______ m/s.
questions.explanation: $\omega=200\pi$ rad/s and $k=\frac{\pi}{150}$ cm⁻¹, so $v=\frac\omega k=200\times150=30000$ cm/s $=300$ m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two short electric dipoles A and B having dipole moment $p_1$ and $p_2$ respectively are placed with their axis mutually perpendicular as shown in the figure. The resultant electric field at a point $x$ is making an angle of $60^\circ$ with the line joining points O and $x$. The ratio of the dipole moments $p_2/p_1$ is ______.
questions.explanation: Point $x$ is on the axis of A and on the equatorial line of B. $E_A=\frac{2kp_1}{r^3}$ along Ox and $E_B=\frac{kp_2}{r^3}$ perpendicular to it. $\tan60^\circ=\frac{E_B}{E_A}=\frac{p_2}{2p_1}\Rightarrow\frac{p_2}{p_1}=2\sqrt3$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: For the given circuit (shown in part (A)) the time dependent input voltage $v_{in}(t)$ and corresponding output $v_o(t)$ are shown in part (B) and part (C), respectively. Identify the components that are used in the circuit between points X and Y.
questions.explanation: The output is clipped at +5 V in the positive half and at −5 V in the negative half. The given branch (ideal diode + Zener) conducts only in the positive half, clamping at $V_Z=5$ V. To clamp the negative half at −5 V too, X–Y must hold the same pair the other way round — an ideal diode and a 5 V Zener (option 2). A resistor cannot fix the output at a constant level.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: When a coil is placed in a time dependent magnetic field the power dissipated in it is $P$. The number of turns, area of the coil and radius of the coil wire are $N$, $A$ and $r$ respectively. For a second coils number of turns, area of the coil and radius of the coil wire are $2N$, $2A$ and $3r$ respectively. When the first coil is replaced with second coil the power dissipated in it is $\sqrt2\,\alpha P$. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
questions.explanation: $\varepsilon\propto NA$ and $R\propto\frac{N\cdot2\pi a}{\pi r^2}$ with coil radius $a\propto\sqrt A$. So $P=\frac{\varepsilon^2}{R}\propto\frac{N^2A^2r^2}{N\sqrt A}=NA^{3/2}r^2$. Ratio $=2\cdot2^{3/2}\cdot9=36\sqrt2$, so $\alpha=36$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two identical long current carrying wires are bent into the shapes shown in the following figures. If the magnitude of magnetic fields at the centres P and Q of a semicircular arc are $B_1$ and $B_2$ respectively, then the ratio $\dfrac{B_1}{B_2}$ is ______.
questions.explanation: (I): two semi-infinite wires ending level with P, each $\frac{\mu_0I}{4\pi r}$, plus the semicircle $\frac{\mu_0I}{4r}$, all in the same direction: $B_1=\frac{\mu_0I}{4\pi r}(2+\pi)$. (II): one semi-infinite wire gives $\frac{\mu_0I}{4\pi r}$, the semicircle $\frac{\mu_0I}{4r}$, and the downward wire passes through Q's line, giving zero: $B_2=\frac{\mu_0I}{4\pi r}(1+\pi)$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: For a thin symmetric prism made of glass (refractive index 1.5), the ratio of incident angle and minimum deviation will be ______.
questions.explanation: Thin prism: $\delta_m=(\mu-1)A=0.5A$. At minimum deviation $i=\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}=0.75A$. So $i:\delta_m=0.75:0.5=3:2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Refer the figure given below. $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ are refractive indices of air and lens material. The height of image will be ______ cm.
questions.explanation: Refraction at one spherical surface: $\frac{\mu_2}{v}-\frac{\mu_1}{u}=\frac{\mu_2-\mu_1}{R}$ with $u=-40$ cm, $R=-20$ cm: $\frac{1.54}{v}=-0.027-0.025\Rightarrow v\approx-29.6$ cm. $m=\frac{\mu_1v}{\mu_2u}=\frac{-29.6}{1.54\times(-40)}\approx0.48$, so image height $\approx2\times0.48\approx1$ cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.text: For a certain metal, when monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$ is incident, the stopping potential for photoelectrons is $3V_0$. When the same metal is illuminated by light of wavelength $2\lambda$, then the stopping potential becomes $V_0$. The threshold wavelength for photoelectric emission for the given metal is $\alpha\lambda$. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
questions.explanation: $3eV_0=\frac{hc}{\lambda}-\phi$ and $eV_0=\frac{hc}{2\lambda}-\phi$. Subtracting: $eV_0=\frac{hc}{4\lambda}$, so $\phi=\frac{hc}{2\lambda}-\frac{hc}{4\lambda}=\frac{hc}{4\lambda}$ and $\lambda_0=4\lambda$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An electromagnetic wave travelling in $x$-direction is described by field equation $E_y=300\sin\omega\left(t-\dfrac xc\right)$. If the electron is restricted to move in $y$-direction only with speed of $1.5\times10^6$ m/s then ratio of maximum electric and magnetic forces acting on the electron is ______.
questions.explanation: $F_E=eE_0$ and $F_B=evB_0=\frac{evE_0}{c}$, so $\frac{F_E}{F_B}=\frac cv=\frac{3\times10^8}{1.5\times10^6}=200$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Angular momentum of an electron in a hydrogen atom is $\dfrac{3h}{\pi}$, then the energy of the electron is ______ eV.
questions.explanation: $\frac{nh}{2\pi}=\frac{3h}{\pi}\Rightarrow n=6$. $E_6=-\frac{13.6}{36}\approx-0.38$ eV.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Mechanical Properties of Solids and Fluids
questions.text: A liquid drop of diameter 2 mm breaks into 512 droplets. The change in surface energy is $\alpha\times10^{-6}$ J. The value of $\alpha$ is ______. (Take surface tension of liquid = 0.08 N/m)
questions.explanation: Volume conserved: $r=\frac{R}{8}$ with $R=1$ mm. New area $=512\cdot4\pi\frac{R^2}{64}=8\cdot4\pi R^2$, so $\Delta A=7\cdot4\pi R^2$. $\Delta E=T\Delta A=0.08\times7\times4\pi\times10^{-6}\approx7\times10^{-6}$ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In single slit diffraction pattern, the wavelength of light used is 628 nm and slit width is 0.2 mm, the angular width of central maximum is $\alpha\times10^{-2}$ degrees. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
questions.explanation: Angular width $=\frac{2\lambda}{a}=\frac{2\times628\times10^{-9}}{0.2\times10^{-3}}=6.28\times10^{-3}$ rad $=6.28\times10^{-3}\times\frac{180}{\pi}\approx0.36^\circ=36\times10^{-2}$ degrees.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A vessel contains 0.15 m³ of a gas at pressure 8 bar and temperature 140 °C with $c_p=3R$ and $c_v=2R$. It is expanded adiabatically till pressure falls to 1 bar. The work done during this process is ______ kJ. (R is gas constant)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: 1 μC charge moving with velocity $\vec v=\left(\hat i-2\hat j+3\hat k\right)$ m/s in the region of magnetic field $\vec B=\left(2\hat i+3\hat j-5\hat k\right)$ T. The magnitude of force acting on it is $\sqrt\alpha\times10^{-6}$ N. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Mechanical Properties of Solids and Fluids
questions.text: A uniform wire of length $l$ of weight $w$ is suspended from the roof with a weight of $W$ at the other end. The stress in the wire at $\frac l3$ distance from the top is $\left(\dfrac WA+\dfrac{2}{\gamma}\dfrac wA\right)$, where $A$ is the cross sectional area of the wire. The value of $\gamma$ is ______.
questions.explanation: At $\frac l3$ from the top, the wire supports $W$ plus the wire below it, $\frac23w$. Stress $=\frac{W+\frac23w}{A}$, so $\gamma=3$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Mechanical Properties of Solids and Fluids
questions.text: A tub is filled with water and a wooden cube 10 cm × 10 cm × 10 cm is placed in the water. The wooden cube is found to float on the water with a part of it submerged in water. When a metal coin is placed on the wooden cube, the submerged part is increased by 3.87 cm. The mass of the metal coin is ______ gram. (Take water density as 1 g/cm³ and density of wood as 0.4 g/cm³)
questions.explanation: Extra buoyancy equals the coin's weight: $m=\rho_w\times(10\times10\times3.87)=387$ g. (Initially 4 cm is under water, so 7.87 cm < 10 cm — the cube still floats.)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The mass of iron converted into $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$ by the action of 18 g of steam is: (Given: Molar mass of H, O and Fe are 1, 16 and 56 g mol⁻¹ respectively) Assume iron is present in excess:
questions.explanation: $3\mathrm{Fe}+4\mathrm{H_2O}\to\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}+4\mathrm{H_2}$. 18 g steam = 1 mol, which reacts with $\frac34$ mol Fe $=\frac34\times56=42$ g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What is the energy (in J atom⁻¹) required for the following process? $\mathrm{Li^{2+}(g)\to Li^{3+}(g)+e^-}$ (Take the ionization energy for the H atom in the ground state as $2.18\times10^{-18}$ J atom⁻¹)
questions.explanation: $\mathrm{Li^{2+}}$ is hydrogen-like with $Z=3$: $IE=Z^2\times2.18\times10^{-18}=9\times2.18\times10^{-18}=1.962\times10^{-17}$ J.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement (I): The correct sequence of bond lengths in the following species is $\mathrm{O_2^+<O_2<O_2^-<O_2^{2-}}$. Statement (II): The correct sequence of number of unpaired electrons in the following species is $\mathrm{O_2>O_2^+>O_2^->O_2^{2-}}$. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Bond orders: $\mathrm{O_2^+}$ 2.5, $\mathrm{O_2}$ 2, $\mathrm{O_2^-}$ 1.5, $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$ 1 — bond length rises as bond order falls, so (I) is true. Unpaired electrons: 1, 2, 1, 0 for $\mathrm{O_2^+,O_2,O_2^-,O_2^{2-}}$; $\mathrm{O_2^+}$ and $\mathrm{O_2^-}$ are equal, so (II) is false.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Consider the following data. (i) $\mathrm{2Al(s)+6HCl(aq)\to Al_2Cl_6(aq)+3H_2(g)}$ + 1200 kJ/mol (ii) $\mathrm{H_2(g)+Cl_2(g)\to2HCl(g)}$ + 164 kJ/mol (iii) $\mathrm{HCl(g)+aq\to HCl(aq)}$ + 83 kJ/mol (iv) $\mathrm{Al_2Cl_6(s)+aq\to Al_2Cl_6(aq)}$ + 663 kJ/mol. The enthalpy of formation of anhydrous solid $\mathrm{Al_2Cl_6}$ is:
questions.explanation: Heat released means $\Delta H$ is negative. Target $\mathrm{2Al+3Cl_2\to Al_2Cl_6(s)}$ = (i) + 3(ii) + 6(iii) − (iv): $-1200-492-498+663=-1527$ kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: 19.5 g of fluoro acetic acid (molar mass = 78 g mol⁻¹) is dissolved in 500 g of water at 298 K. The depression in the freezing point of water was 1 °C. What is $K_a$ of fluoro acetic acid? (For water, $K_f$ = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹). Assume molarity and molality to have same values.
questions.explanation: Molality $m=\frac{19.5/78}{0.5}=0.5$. From $\Delta T_f=iK_fm$: $1=i\times1.86\times0.5$, so $i\approx1.075$ and $\alpha=i-1\approx0.075$. $K_a=\frac{c\alpha^2}{1-\alpha}=\frac{0.5\times0.0057}{0.925}\approx3\times10^{-3}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The solubility product constants of $\mathrm{Ag_2CrO_4}$ and AgBr are $32x$ and $4y$ respectively at 298 K. The value of $\left(\dfrac{\text{molarity of }\mathrm{Ag_2CrO_4}}{\text{molarity of AgBr}}\right)$ can be expressed as:
questions.explanation: $\mathrm{Ag_2CrO_4}$: $4s^3=32x\Rightarrow s=2\sqrt[3]x$. AgBr: $s'^2=4y\Rightarrow s'=2\sqrt y$. Ratio $=\frac{\sqrt[3]x}{\sqrt y}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: An electrochemical cell is constructed using half cells in the direction of spontaneous change: $\mathrm{Fe(OH)_2(s)+2e^-\to Fe(s)+2OH^-(aq)}$, $E^\circ=-0.88$ V and $\mathrm{AgBr(s)+e^-\to Ag(s)+Br^-(aq)}$, $E^\circ=+0.07$ V. Which of the following option is correct?
questions.explanation: The AgBr/Ag couple has the higher $E^\circ$, so it is the cathode; Fe is oxidised to $\mathrm{Fe(OH)_2}$ at the anode. $E^\circ_{cell}=0.07-(-0.88)=+0.95$ V (intensive). The overall reaction is the one in option 1.
options: Fe is reduced in the electrochemical cell

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: $t_{100\%}$ is the time required for the 100% completion of the reaction while $t_{1/2}$ is the time required for 50% of the reaction to be completed. Which of the following option correctly represents the relation between $t_{100\%}$ and $t_{1/2}$ for zero and first order reactions respectively?
questions.explanation: Zero order: $t_{100\%}=\frac{[A]_0}{k}=2t_{1/2}$. First order: $t=\frac1k\ln\frac{[A]_0}{[A]}$ becomes infinite as $[A]\to0$, so a first-order reaction never completes — written here as $(t_{1/2})^\infty$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement (I): The first ionisation enthalpy of the elements Na, Mg, Cl and Ar follows the order Na > Mg > Cl > Ar. Statement (II): Among Ca, Al, Fe and B, the third ionisation enthalpy is very high for Ca. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Ionisation enthalpy rises across period 3, so the order is Ar > Cl > Mg > Na — (I) is false. $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$ has a noble-gas configuration, so removing a third electron is very hard — (II) is true.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement (I): Oxidising power of halogens decreases in the order $\mathrm{F_2>Cl_2>Br_2>I_2}$, which is the basis of “Layer test”. Statement (II): “Layer test” to identify $\mathrm{Br_2}$ and $\mathrm{I_2}$ in aqueous solution involves the oxidation of bromide or iodide into $\mathrm{Br_2}$ or $\mathrm{I_2}$ respectively with $\mathrm{Cl_2}$, which is a type of displacement redox reaction. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Oxidising power does fall from $\mathrm{F_2}$ to $\mathrm{I_2}$, and that is why chlorine water displaces $\mathrm{Br_2}$/$\mathrm{I_2}$ from bromide/iodide in the layer test (orange/violet layer). Both statements are true.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following sets includes all the species that will change the orange colour of $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$ in acidic medium?
questions.explanation: Acidified dichromate (orange) turns green ($\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$) only with reducing agents. $\mathrm{Fe^{2+},Sn^{2+},I^-,S^{2-}}$ are all reducing; each other set contains a species already in its highest usual state ($\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{Sn^{4+}}$, $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Match List - I (Chromium (III) Complexes, en = ethylene diamine) with List - II ($\Delta_0$ in cm⁻¹). A. $\mathrm{[Cr(CN)_6]^{3-}}$ B. $\mathrm{[CrF_6]^{3-}}$ C. $\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}$ D. $\mathrm{[Cr(en)_3]^{3+}}$ — I. 15,060 II. 17,400 III. 22,300 IV. 26,600. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Spectrochemical series: $\mathrm{CN^->en>H_2O>F^-}$. So $\mathrm{CN^-}$ 26,600 (IV), en 22,300 (III), $\mathrm{H_2O}$ 17,400 (II), $\mathrm{F^-}$ 15,060 (I).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement (I): 1,2,3-Trihydroxypropane can be separated from water by simple distillation. Statement (II): An azeotropic mixture cannot be separated by fractional distillation. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Glycerol (1,2,3-trihydroxypropane) decomposes at its boiling point, so it is purified by distillation under reduced pressure, not simple distillation — (I) is false. An azeotrope boils at constant composition, so fractional distillation cannot separate it — (II) is true.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement (I): Benzyl chloride reacts faster in $S_N1$ mechanism than ethyl chloride. Statement (II): Ethyl carbocation intermediate is less stabilized by hyperconjugation than benzyl carbocation by resonance. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: The benzyl carbocation is resonance-stabilised over the ring, far more than the ethyl carbocation is by hyperconjugation, so benzyl chloride ionises faster by $S_N1$. Both statements are true.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In IUPAC nomenclature, the correct order of decreasing priority of functional group is:
questions.explanation: Priority order: acid > ester > acid halide > amide > nitrile > aldehyde > ketone > alcohol > amine > alkene/alkyne. Only option 3 follows it (option 2 puts ester below amide; option 4 puts nitrile below aldehyde).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For the given molecule, “$x$”, the preferred site for the attack of the electrophile is:
questions.explanation: The ring on the carbonyl side is deactivated by C=O. The ring on nitrogen is activated (–NHCOPh is an o,p-director, though weaker than –NH₂); the bulky group hinders the ortho position s, so attack is mainly para — at u.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Match List - I (Mixture of Compounds) with List - II (Reagent used to distinguish). A. Diethyl amine + Ethyl amine B. Acetaldehyde + Acetone C. Ethanol + Phenol D. Benzoic acid + Cinnamic acid — I. Bromine water II. $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ + KOH, Δ III. Neutral $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$ IV. Ammonical silver nitrate. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: A: carbylamine test (II) works only for the primary amine. B: Tollens' reagent (IV) is reduced by the aldehyde, not the ketone. C: neutral $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$ (III) gives violet colour with phenol. D: cinnamic acid's C=C decolourises bromine water (I).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Consider the three aromatic molecules (P, Q and R) whose structures have been given below. The correct order regarding the reactivity of these compounds with $\mathrm{Ph-\overset{+}{N}{\equiv}N\,Cl^-}$ under optimum but slightly acidic medium is:
questions.explanation: Azo coupling needs the –NMe₂ lone pair in conjugation with the ring. Ortho-methyl groups twist –NMe₂ out of the ring plane (steric inhibition of resonance): one in Q, two in R. Activation falls P > Q > R.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Match List - I (Vitamin) with List - II (Name). A. Vitamin $B_1$ B. Vitamin $B_2$ C. Vitamin $B_6$ D. Vitamin C — I. Pyridoxine II. Ascorbic acid III. Thiamine IV. Riboflavin. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: $B_1$ = thiamine, $B_2$ = riboflavin, $B_6$ = pyridoxine, C = ascorbic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A salt with few drops of conc. HCl gives apple green colour in flame test. The group precipitate of the salt is dissolved in acetic acid and treated with $\mathrm{K_2CrO_4}$ to give yellow precipitate. When the sodium carbonate extract of the salt solution is heated with conc. $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ and ammonium molybdate, it resulted a canary yellow precipitate. The cation and anion present in the salt are respectively,
questions.explanation: Apple-green flame and yellow $\mathrm{BaCrO_4}$ with $\mathrm{K_2CrO_4}$ point to $\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}$. A canary-yellow precipitate with ammonium molybdate in $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ is the test for phosphate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: 5.33 g of $\mathrm{CrCl_3\cdot6H_2O}$, which is a 1 : 3 electrolyte, is dissolved in water and is passed through a cation exchanger. The chloride ions in the eluted solution, on treatment with $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ results in 8.61 g of AgCl. The ratio of moles of complex reacted and moles of AgCl formed is ______ $\times10^{-2}$. (Nearest integer) [Molar mass in g mol⁻¹ Cr : 52, Ag : 108, Cl : 35.5, H : 1, O : 16]
questions.explanation: Molar mass $=266.5$, so complex $=\frac{5.33}{266.5}=0.02$ mol. AgCl $=\frac{8.61}{143.5}=0.06$ mol (all three Cl⁻ are ionic, $\mathrm{[Cr(H_2O)_6]Cl_3}$). Ratio $=\frac{0.02}{0.06}=0.33=33\times10^{-2}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Consider the isomers of hydrocarbon with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_5H_{10}}$. These isomers do not decolourise $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ solution. These isomers are subjected to chlorination with chlorine in presence of light to give monochloro compounds. The total number of monochloro compounds (structural isomers only) formed is ______.
questions.explanation: Not decolourising $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ means cycloalkanes: cyclopentane (1 monochloro product), methylcyclobutane (4), ethylcyclopropane (4), 1,1-dimethylcyclopropane (2), 1,2-dimethylcyclopropane (3). Total $=14$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: One mole of an alkane (x) requires 8 mole oxygen for complete combustion. Sum of number of carbon and hydrogen atoms in the alkane (x) is ______.
questions.explanation: $\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}}$ needs $\frac{3n+1}{2}$ mol $\mathrm{O_2}$. $\frac{3n+1}{2}=8\Rightarrow n=5$: $\mathrm{C_5H_{12}}$, so $5+12=17$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: For reaction A → P, rate constant $k=1.5\times10^3$ s⁻¹ at 27 °C. If activation energy for the above reaction is 60 kJ mol⁻¹, then the temperature (in °C) at which rate constant, $k=4.5\times10^3$ s⁻¹ is ______. (Nearest integer) Given: log 2 = 0.30, log 3 = 0.48, R = 8.3 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, ln 10 = 2.3
questions.explanation: $\log\frac{k_2}{k_1}=\frac{E_a}{2.3R}\left(\frac1{T_1}-\frac1{T_2}\right)$: $0.48=\frac{60000}{2.3\times8.3}\left(\frac1{300}-\frac1{T_2}\right)\Rightarrow T_2\approx314$ K $\approx41$ °C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: At the transition temperature T, $\mathrm{A\rightleftharpoons B}$ and $\Delta G^0=105-35\log T$ where A and B are two states of substance X. The transition temperature in °C when pressure is 1 atm is ______. (Nearest integer)
questions.explanation: At the transition temperature the two states are in equilibrium, so $\Delta G^0=0$: $\log T=3\Rightarrow T=1000$ K $=727$ °C.
